prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Could you help me find a white wine that isn't too heavy?"

List A:
Wine 1: Pinot Grigio, Italy, $14. Tasting note: "Lightweight and thin in the mouth, this zesty white wine does a good job of keeping your palate refreshed and quenches your thirst (think hot summer day). It's an easy and informal wine that stays focused on simplicity."
Wine 2: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $18. Tasting note: "This is a slightly grassy, green white wine that fans of this style may enjoy; others not so much. Light in alcohol, it has medium body and crispness."
Wine 3: White Blend, Australia, $14. Tasting note: "Thick and pulpy on the palate, this white is fruity and simple, with pear, melon and citrus aromas and flavors. It's surprisingly heavy for such a low-alcohol (12.7%) wine."
Wine 4: Fiano, Italy, $21. Tasting note: "This is a light and friendly white wine that would pair well with salads and vegetarian dishes. The wine has easygoing aromas of yellow fruit and some dusty mineral tones for extra dimension. A Marc de Grazia selection, various American importers."
Wine 5: Pinot Gris, US, $9. Tasting note: "Light and grapefruity, without much Pinot Gris character. An innocuous, fairly generic white wine."

List B:
Wine 1: Fiano, US, $26. Tasting note: "This is an interesting, dry white wine from an unusual grape variety. It's more savory than fruity, as the aromas resemble white and black pepper, while flavors are subtle and figgy. The texture is quite rich and the finish lingers nicely. It's very full-bodied for a white, and definitely worth a try."
Wine 2: Cortese, US, $18. Tasting note: "A little heavy and soft for a white wine, but shows true dryness and some interestingly earthy flavors of white tobacco, herbs and citrus fruits. Promising, but needs greater structure and complexity."
Wine 3: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $15. Tasting note: "Here's a wine that will surprise you. It has real richness and varietal flavor, and is dry and balanced, with the weight you want in a nice Cabernet. Might even get a little better in another year or two."
Wine 4: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $15. Tasting note: "This is an innocuous, flowery and lemony white wine priced to sell that offers a creamy texture amid a light body and soul. For picnics and larger gatherings, it'll represent well."
Wine 5: Pinot Grigio, US, $10. Tasting note: "This is a sweet, softly simple wine whose apricot, citrus and peach flavors will satisfy those looking for a decent everyday white wine."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
